key_insight: DAGO treats workflow parent selection as a contextual bandit problem, using LinUCB to learn which multi-parent fusions are most likely to produce better child workflows under a tight evaluation budget.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to reduce expensive search in agentic workflow optimization by reusing and recombining successful designs instead of exploring blindly.
method: Represent each candidate parent set as a bandit arm using pretrained embeddings of workflow code and prompts.
Select arms with diagonal LinUCB to balance exploitation of promising fusions and exploration of uncertain ones.
Use an LLM to fuse selected parents into a child workflow, then update the bandit with the child’s validation score.
evidence_signal: Across six benchmarks, DAGO achieved the best macro-average score and improved AFlow from 80.3 to 81.7 while reducing aggregate search expenditure by 11.2%.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and stability of pretrained embeddings and LLM-generated fusion, so gains may be sensitive to representation choices and prompt design.
paper_title: Fusion is the New Mutation: Bandit-Guided Evolution on Workflow Graphs
